advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the missing advisory/ratchet/strict enforcement modes with the ticket ACs — either implement per-shard modes in the manifest/driver/docs or amend the ticket to match the single-mode design actually shipped.
evidence: Ticket plan: 'an explicit per-shard enforcement mode: advisory / ratchet / strict' and ACs '[x] Manifest loading accepts only advisory, ratchet, or strict', '[x] Advisory ...', '[x] Ratchet ...', '[x] Strict ...' — all checked.
`.github/mutation-shards.toml` shard rows contain only name/source/tests/support/survivors_max/no_tests_max/timeouts_max/score_floor/equivalent_fingerprints — no `mode`.
search_files docs/mutation-testing.md 'ratchet' -> (no matches); search_files tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py 'advisory' -> (no matches).
scripts/mutation_gate.py:139-149 constructs Shard without any mode; evaluate_runs (l.240) applies a single fixed comparison regardless of shard.
advisory.finding: The phased enforcement model (advisory/ratchet/strict modes) that is the core of the ticket plan and appears in nearly every acceptance criterion is entirely absent: the manifest has no `mode` field, the `Shard` dataclass and `load_manifest` never read one, and the driver applies one unconditional comparison (always archive+run base, always compare killed->non-killed for AST-identical units, always apply head budgets). The doc and test file contain no mention of advisory/ratchet/strict either.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either implement the selector-derived per-shard matrix (one 30-minute job per shard) as the ticket requires, or justify and document the single serial job and its total-runtime bound.
evidence: _mutation.yml defines one job `mutation` with `timeout-minutes: 30` and a single step `uv run ... scripts/mutation_gate.py run ... --all-shards`; there is no `strategy: matrix` over shards.
run_gate iterates `for name in names:` running `_extract_ref` + `execute_shard` for base and head of every selected shard within the one job (scripts/mutation_gate.py:504-...).

Ticket AC: '[x] Workflows use selector-derived per-shard matrix jobs with a 30-minute limit each'; completion comment claims '_mutation.yml:32-115 derives the shard matrix ... caps each job at 30 minutes'.
Ticket correction comment: 'A single 30-minute base+head all-shard job is also not credibly bounded.'
advisory.finding: The reusable workflow runs a single `mutation` job that invokes `mutation_gate.py run` once (which loops over ALL selected shards serially, archiving base+head per shard) under one 30-minute cap — not the selector-derived per-shard matrix with a 30-minute limit EACH that the ticket AC and completion comment require. The weekly sweep passes `--all-shards`, running all seven shards' base+head archives inside one 30-minute job, exactly the 'single 30-minute base+head all-shard job is not credibly bounded' condition the ticket flagged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reject bool in manifest integer/float budget validation (e.g. `and not isinstance(value, bool)`).
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py:131 `if not all(isinstance(value, int) and value >= 0 for value in budgets)`
scripts/mutation_gate.py:137 `if not isinstance(score_floor, (int, float)) or not 0 < float(score_floor) <= 100`
A shard authored with `survivors_max = true` would be silently accepted as budget 1 rather than rejected as a mis-typed value.
advisory.finding: Manifest integer-budget and score_floor validation treats TOML booleans as valid because bool is an int subclass: `isinstance(True, int)` and `isinstance(True, (int, float))` are both True, so `survivors_max = true` validates as 1 and `score_floor = true` passes `0 < 1.0 <= 100`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct test for function_hashes/unit_name: identical function bodies at different line offsets hash equal; a behavior-changing edit hashes differently; and unit_name strips the __mutmut_N suffix.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py defines `def function_hashes(root, source)` computing `ast.dump(node, annotate_fields=False)` digests and `def unit_name(mutant_name)` stripping the mutmut suffix
search of tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py for `function_hashes` and `unit_name` returns (no matches)
compare_runs/evaluate_runs tests supply unit_hashes literally (e.g. hashes={"pkg.x_f": "same"}), so the actual AST-hash + unit-name derivation is never run against real source
advisory.finding: function_hashes() and unit_name() — the AST-based unit classifier that decides which mutation units count as 'unchanged' and therefore fall under the strict killed->non-killed regression check — have no direct test. A regression that makes the hash sensitive to line numbers/formatting (or otherwise mis-classifies an edited unit as unchanged, or vice versa) would silently disable or misfire the central anti-weakening contract, and every existing comparison test feeds hashes in by hand ({"pkg.x_f": "same"}) so the real hashing code is never exercised.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests asserting load_manifest raises GateError for at least: wrong version, duplicate source, negative budget, and score_floor outside (0,100].
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py load_manifest raises GateError on `raw.get("version") != 1`, non-list shards, `name in shards`, `source in sources`, non-negative-int budgets, and `not 0 < float(score_floor) <= 100`
search of tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py for `GateError` returns (no matches)
advisory.finding: load_manifest's validation branches are untested. It raises GateError for a wrong version, non-list/empty shards, duplicate or empty name/source, negative count budgets, and out-of-range score_floor, but no test drives any invalid manifest; only the valid canonical manifest and valid synthetic manifests are loaded.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for _diagnose_non_killed asserting label='nondeterminism' on a changed rerun and that the gate outcome stays failure.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py: `return "nondeterminism" if changed else "stable"` and run_gate sets `failed = True` before diagnosing
docs/mutation-testing.md: 'a changed outcome is labeled nondeterministic, but the gate remains red'
no test in tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py references _diagnose_non_killed or the 'nondeterminism'/'stable' labels
advisory.finding: The nondeterminism-diagnosis behavior (_diagnose_non_killed reruns non-killed head mutants once and labels the outcome 'nondeterminism' vs 'stable') is untested. The docs promise 'a changed outcome is labeled nondeterministic, but the gate remains red'; no test pins that the diagnostic label is derived correctly or that a changed rerun does not flip the gate to pass.

test_head_budget_failures parametrize cases are only zero-mutants, not checked (unexpected-status), no tests, timeout
